sections.content:
24,095 people

were counted on the census as "sales related occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work have sales occupations not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "sales related occupations (other)", 16.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sales related occupations (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sales related occupations (other)" included:

  • collector salespersons and credit agents
  • estate agents and auctioneers
  • engineering technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sales related occupations (other)" there were more men than women (56.9% compared with 43.1%).

This means "sales related occupations (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 56.9% and women made up 43.1% of "sales related occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sales related occupations (other)" included:

  • financial managers and directors
  • research and development (r&d) managers
  • business and financial project management professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sales related occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "sales related occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sales related occupations (other)", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.1% compared with 28.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (85.1%) than self-employed (14.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
